Verified_Outcome: Tier 3 primary-abstract disposition: Diosmetin inhibited formation of both 1′- and 4-hydroxymidazolam in human liver microsomes in a concentration-dependent manner. The abstract gives apparent Ki values in a jointly reported 30–50 μmol range for diosmetin and luteolin, but does not assign an individual value or state a denominator in the accessible display; this range is retained as source wording and is not assigned to diosmetin alone. Recombinant CYP3A4, but not CYP3A5, showed decreased 1′-hydroxymidazolam formation; both recombinant enzymes showed decreased 4-hydroxymidazolam formation.
Remaining_Limitation: Tier 3 abstract-only review. The apparent Ki range is jointly reported for diosmetin and luteolin, not assigned individually; the accessible abstract display gives μmol without an explicit denominator. Full-text assay conditions, individual Ki estimates, sample details and tested lot/purity remain unverified. No human administration or ordinary-food exposure was studied; no clinical interaction magnitude can be inferred.
